description: We are CYSA Sphere — four young women in STEM uniting computer science, geophysics, sensory engineering, and accessible design. Inspired by NASA’s Earth Information Center, we designed and engineered an interactive physical-and-digital museum exhibit for visually impaired kids: transforming complex orbital datasets (sea surface temperature, lightning strikes, night lights, and forest canopies) into intuitive acoustic, thermal, and haptic landscapes.
summary:
Earth Jukebox is an accessible, multisensory museum exhibit developed by CYSA Sphere that translates open NASA Earth observation data into a tactile and auditory learning experience for blind, low-vision, and sighted children.
We developed an ergonomic, child-height (65 cm) physical kiosk featuring a 60 cm tactile relief globe, an East/West rotational joystick that simulates Earth’s day/night cycle while maintaining polar orientation, high-contrast Braille keys, and an interactive touch-to-sonify tablet. Rather than abstract beeps, our live Web Audio engine translates four NASA Scientific Visualization Studio datasets into phenomenon-literal soundscapes: ocean waves for sea temperature (SVS 3912), rolling thunder for lightning (SVS 5011), canopy wind for forest height (SVS 4950), and music-box chimes for night lights (SVS 5276), paired with intelligent, context-aware spoken guidance.
Earth observation has historically relied on visual satellite maps, excluding visually impaired learners. Earth Jukebox breaks this barrier by turning planetary science into a tactile and acoustic symphony. By making Earth data inclusive, playful, and developmentally intuitive, we inspire every young explorer—regardless of visual ability—to build spatial mental models of our living planet and pursue STEM literacy.
details:
Earth Jukebox transforms NASA satellite Earth observation data into a physical, multisensory exhibit for blind, low-vision, and sighted children in science museums and schools. The project centers on a child-height (65 cm) interactive kiosk featuring a 60 cm tactile relief globe with etched coastlines, jumbo high-contrast Braille keys, and a 1-axis East/West joystick that preserves polar orientation while simulating Earth's rotation and day/night cycle.

Instead of abstract beeps or relying solely on visual satellite imagery, Earth Jukebox uses a custom Web Audio engine to convert open NASA Scientific Visualization Studio datasets into intuitive, phenomenon-literal soundscapes: warm ocean wave chords for sea surface temperature (SVS 3912), rolling thunder for lightning flash density (SVS 5011), rustling canopy frequencies for forest height (SVS 4950), and music-box chimes for nighttime city illumination (SVS 5276). A synchronized companion tablet plays 48-frame multi-temporal NASA image sequences, allowing children to probe geographic regions and hear the intensity of natural phenomena crescendo or soften in real time, accompanied by context-aware spoken descriptions that guide them across continents and oceans.

Developed by CYSA Sphere using TypeScript, React 19, TanStack Start, Three.js, React Three Fiber, Globe.gl, and a Python/FFmpeg data pipeline, the project bridges space science and universal design. By prioritizing pediatric ergonomics, tactile mental mapping, spatial stereo audio, and full WAI-ARIA screen-reader harmony, Earth Jukebox removes visual barriers to planetary literacy, empowering all young learners to experience, understand, and protect our living planet.
